title: Physics on arXiv | 22 November 2026 announcement batch | 6 notable papers
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This is an inferred ranking; the candidate pool recorded no external-attention matches and citation evidence is limited for papers only days old. Treat the entries as notable recent papers, not a popularity list.

sections.title: Disentangling Lengthscales in Disordered Fracture
sections.abstract: The authors use a two-dimensional random fuse model to distinguish the disorder-dependent screening length of crack-tip damage from the length in Bažant's size-effect law, and propose pre-failure microfracture percolation as a possible origin of the latter.
sections.claimed_result: In simulations, the statistical fracture-process-zone length scales approximately as disorder strength to the first power, while the size-effect-law length and crack extension scale near disorder strength to the 1.34 power; the authors suggest percolation of microfractures may explain the latter.
sections.evidence_type: computational; two-dimensional Weibull-disordered random fuse simulations and a coarse-grained load-redistribution model
sections.unique_caveat: An idealized 2D model rather than a measurement on real materials; origins and scaling of damage zones, particularly in more brittle regimes, remain open.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate-pool score 1.00, the highest among selected papers, entirely from four cross-lists (4 × 0.25).

sections.title: Bayesian Quantum Thermometry of Ultracold Gases with Non-Equilibrium Single-Atom Probes
sections.abstract: The authors experimentally infer an ultracold bath's temperature from non-equilibrium spin-exchange dynamics of single-atom probes and find that adaptive Bayesian measurement reaches a prescribed precision with 2.5 times fewer measurements than an unoptimized protocol.
sections.claimed_result: Adaptive expected-information-gain measurements reduce the number of measurements needed for a target precision by a factor of 2.5 versus the unoptimized protocol, with estimates compared against time-of-flight references.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; individually measured 133Cs probe atoms in a thermal 87Rb bath, Bayesian spin-population inference, and time-of-flight references
sections.unique_caveat: The inference uses an independently measured bath atom number and a model of spin-exchange rates; information efficiency trades off against setup-specific control and measurement overhead.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate-pool score 0.75 from three cross-lists; supporting data are openly deposited at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24390998, which is context rather than a score component.

sections.title: Molecular structure breaks universality in screening behavior of electrolyte solutions
sections.abstract: Using machine-learned classical density functional theory, the authors find that solvent polarity, solvent attraction, and ionic structure change screening modes and exponents, challenging a universal scaling law across concentrated electrolyte models.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that solvent attraction can introduce a monotonic decay mode, solvent polarity can produce re-entrant screening, and ionic structure can alter screening exponents; they conclude no single scaling law applies across their molecularly distinct models.
sections.evidence_type: computational; machine-learned classical density functional theory applied to electrolyte models with increasing solvent and ionic detail
sections.unique_caveat: Model-based calculations rather than a new measurement; correspondence between the model hierarchy and specific real solutions needs experimental testing.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate-pool score 0.75 from three cross-lists; it addresses a live disagreement over concentrated-electrolyte screening using a hierarchy of model complexity.

sections.title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
sections.abstract: The author formulates a warm-vapor Rydberg receiver as an intensity-modulated optical link and derives its RF link-budget metrics from a velocity-averaged four-level atomic response, while finding its noise figure limits general antenna replacement.
sections.claimed_result: For a rubidium transition at 17.04 GHz, closed-form estimates agree with a velocity-resolved density-matrix model to 1% for slope and intercepts and 10% for bandwidth; they underestimate group delay by about one-third.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; closed-form warm-vapor response compared with a velocity-resolved density-matrix model
sections.unique_caveat: The paper's analysis says the warm-vapor noise figure rules out the receiver as a general substitute for a conventional antenna and low-noise amplifier.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate-pool score 0.75 from three cross-lists; includes quantitative model comparisons for a cross-field sensing device.

sections.title: Optimised 8th-Order Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Quantum Simulation
sections.abstract: The authors construct optimized general eighth-order product formulas for quantum dynamics, benchmark them on a Heisenberg XZ chain, and simulate noisy circuits to assess when the schemes could outperform lower-order alternatives.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report improved theoretical efficiency over prior state-of-the-art schemes and find their recommended formulas become competitive as hardware noise falls toward fault-tolerant levels.
sections.evidence_type: computational; product-formula analysis, Heisenberg XZ-chain simulations, and simulated noisy circuits using qiskit-omelyan
sections.unique_caveat: At the noise levels modeled as current, the Leapfrog scheme remains the best choice; proposed gains are not demonstrated on quantum hardware.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate-pool score 0.75 from three cross-lists; includes a many-body benchmark and noisy-circuit comparison.

sections.title: Neural variational Skyrmions as a topological benchmark: emergent symmetry, precision energies and KAN--MLP comparison
sections.abstract: Neural variational optimization produces three-dimensional Skyrmions with charges 1–4 without a symmetry ansatz, recovers familiar shapes, and compares Kolmogorov–Arnold networks with multilayer perceptrons across more than a thousand training runs.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report spontaneous emergence of toroidal, tetrahedral, and cubic solutions, topological-charge errors at most 10^-6 in their highest-precision solutions, and a KAN parameter-efficiency advantage that largely disappears against tuned MLPs.
sections.evidence_type: computational; neural variational Skyrme-model solutions checked against physical constraints, independent quadratures, resolution sweeps, and over 1,000 network-training runs
sections.unique_caveat: Results cover charges 1–4 in this model; the apparent KAN advantage depends on comparison protocol, since tuned MLPs perform at least as well at fixed wall-clock time.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate-pool score 0.75 from three cross-lists; code and data are available at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24390286, a reproducibility signal not included in the score.
